answer: Latency escrow. Each new identity must pre-pay for a fixed window of signed work before its attestations count, and the agent's atlas of prior interactions is queried against a fresh pigment sample tied to a hardware root. Clones pay the escrow, wait out the window, and still fail the sample cross-check, forfeiting the deposit to the challenger. A lantern of rotating challenge slots makes every retry cost more than the reward it chases.
